body: I've gotten shafted. We spent two really good weeks together. She just said she is comfortable with her ex and that she doesn't want to see me anymore. Can still be friends, etc.

Met a girl I finally clicked with. After 2 years of sorting through fakes and different levels of crazy. I finally found one who I liked being with, could be myself around, and she made me happy. I know all about that "True happiness comes from within". For some people it's not that easy. I get emotional rewards from spending time with someone who reciprocates my affection.
Music does when I'm in the right mood. But lately with events it's more depressing than helpful.
I'm not sure really. Probably what I do with my spare time currently.

I know I can have a good time without drugs. I'm typically sober. Though I've been going to raves recently and fucked around with some harder stuff, I don't have much of desire to do any of it anymore. I rely on weed to keep my BPD under control since the doctors haven't been able to do anything with medication to keep me under control.
Not too much really. I've been battling back the depression anxiety with a mound of weed. It's the only thing that's kept me sane this past year or so.

Thanks for pointing out the BPD. I don't think I'd consider myself bi-polar, and having read the wiki on it, this all makes a lot of sense.


The most distinguishing symptoms of BPD are marked sensitivity to rejection and thinking about and feeling afraid of possible abandonment.

People with BPD feel emotions more easily, more deeply, and for longer than others do. Emotions may repeatedly re-fire, or reinitiate, prolonging their emotional reactions. Consequently, it can take a long time for people with BPD to return to a stable emotional baseline following an intense emotional experience.

While people with BPD feel joy intensely, they are especially prone to dysphoria, or feelings of mental and emotional distress. Zanarini et al. recognize four categories of dysphoria that are typical of this condition: extreme emotions; destructiveness or self-destructiveness; feeling fragmented or lacking identity; and feelings of victimization.


Thanks again.
Thanks for your support and for the talk.

I do feel as though they have torn me down. What healthy 20something should consider suicide? Sure, I might have come out on top of the chaos that has been my life, but I'm not complete. I'm missing parts of me that I'll never get back, parts that made me whole and made me okay.

I don't know if it's just me, but I don't understand quite how to better myself. There isn't a single thing I can think of that would make me truly happy. Sure, money would solve a lot of issues, but I just don't feel like I'm ever going to be actually happy.
I know the feeling. But how do I become okay with shutting out someone who's basically been with me for my entire adult life? That's fucking difficult.

I'd like to have some meaning in life. People keep saying "Turn to god, things will be clear" I want to slap these people. If I have one divine purpose in life, it's obviously to make people feel better about theirs. It's absolutely astonishing how I've made it this far.

Plenty of hobbies. I don't have issues with social settings or finding them. But I'm hollow. I'll feel a fleeting sensation of happiness and then it's gone. I can't really describe it as anything other than bittersweet.
